summary: FD_TC_210_Denied Boarding | APPR | PAL Flight | PAL as MSL | DDS Behaviour Validation
title: Denied Boarding | APPR | PAL Flight | PAL as MSL | DDS Behaviour Validation
description:
Customer is denied boarding on a PAL-operated flight within an AC-ticketed itinerary. Denied boarding is a distinct disruption type from delay/cancellation. Validates that DDS correctly identifies the denied boarding event on a PAL-operated leg, determines PAL as the MSL, and assesses APPR eligibility. Since PAL coding is known to be spotty, this test also confirms DDS behaviour when the denied boarding reason code from PAL may be missing or incomplete. Denied boarding under APPR has specific compensation tiers and the customer must have been rebooked or chose not to travel.

Prerequisites:
PNR: Single passenger (Antoine Lavoie), multi-leg itinerary. Leg 1: AC 501 YUL?MNL (AC operated, no disruption). Leg 2: PAL 205 MNL?CEB (PAL operated, DENIED BOARDING). Customer was denied boarding on PAL 205 due to overbooking. Customer was rebooked on next available PAL flight: PAL 207 MNL?CEB, arriving 5 hours later. Original Leg 2 scheduled arrival: 14:00. Rebooked arrival: 19:00 (5hr delay at final destination). Denied boarding reason: Overbooking (if PAL coding present). Booking changes: INVOL rebooking after denied boarding. Carrier: AC ticketing carrier, PAL operating carrier on denied boarding leg. 72hrs: Elapsed. Time limit: Within 366 days. No duplicate case. CyberSource: GREEN.
